aria: Animated recap of the Celtics' 131 to 116 road win over the Wizards: Jayson Tatum's driving finger roll with 3:06 left that made it 119 to 112 after Washington had cut a 34-point lead to five, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Tatum's 41 points, the top scorers, how the Celtics won, and the next game at home against Atlanta.

notes: Box score from the Celtics' 131–116 road win over the Washington Wizards on Nov 24, 2026 (NBA Cup group play), from the StatMuse game page (full box score, team stats and scoring play-by-play), with game details from the Associated Press (via TSN and CBS Boston), the Boston Globe, The Sports Leader (KNBR), Boston Celtics On SI, CelticsBlog and Roundtable Sports (via Yahoo Sports) and Ball Exclusives (via Yardbarker). All 131 Boston points and all 116 Washington points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (34–46–24–27 to 28–21–40–27) add up to both totals: 80–49 Boston at the half, 104–89 after three. Threes (22 of 51 to 12 of 36), assists (30–25), free throws made (17–22), points in the paint (44–48), points off turnovers (23–15) and both biggest leads (Boston 34, Washington 2) are from the StatMuse team stats. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Tuesday's games: Boston 12–6 (second in the East), Atlanta 11–6.

Boston snapped a four-game losing streak and is 3–0 in NBA Cup group play; it hosts Atlanta on Friday, Nov 27, and the winner finishes atop the group (AP; The Sports Leader; Roundtable Sports). Washington's three-game winning streak ended and it is out of the Cup (AP). Boston scored 46 in the second quarter with 10 threes (AP) and led 80–46 after Paul George's layup with 21 seconds left in the half (StatMuse play-by-play). Tatum had 28 by halftime (AP). Washington won the third quarter 40–24 and got within 117–112 on AJ Dybantsa's driving bank floater with 3:19 left (StatMuse play-by-play; AP; Boston Celtics On SI). Baylor Scheierman then scored all 8 of his points in the last 2:31, two threes and two free throws (StatMuse play-by-play; Roundtable Sports). Queta's 13 first-quarter points are from AP.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jayson Tatum's driving finger roll, assisted by Paul George, with 3:06 left that made it 119–112 (StatMuse play-by-play; AP: after Dybantsa's bank shot made it 117–112, "Tatum got free for a layup"). Boston outscored Washington 14–4 from there (StatMuse play-by-play). The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Boston Celtics or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Jayson Tatum's listed 6-foot-8 and 229 pounds with No. 0 (Wikipedia), with his arms scaled to the 6-foot-11 wingspan measured at the 2016 Nike Hoop Summit (DraftExpress), in Boston's road green with his proposed look from the site's look sheet (not yet approved). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
